profile.headline: Software Engineer @ M&T Bank
profile.summary:
I'm a Fullstack engineer at M&T Bank, passionate about engineering maintainable solutions and exploring new technologies. My current stack is Angular / .NET / SQL, with previous experience in iOS development. 

I am always open to branching out and learning new technologies, because I firmly believe that continuous development is key to success in technology.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
In July of 2026, I graduated M&T's Technology Development Program, promoted to Software Engineer.

I am currently working as a Fullstack engineer (Angular/.NET) on a team supporting Retail Branch Technology. We recently fully released a modernized experience for unsecured loan applications, a project which started when I joined the team a year ago. This is part of a larger effort to migrate a range of functionalities off of legacy systems, and into the modern application which my team helps to build and support.

positions.title: Associate Software Engineer
positions.description:
I joined M&T's 2 year rotational Technology Development Program, spending my first year on M&T's Mobile Banking team and my second year on a fullstack team supporting Retail Branch Technology.

This past year, I have worked as a fullstack engineer on an Angular / . NET platform which bankers use to service customers in retail branches. Specifically, I helped deliver a new flow to submit a loan application. Implemented within an angular microfrontend, this new flow leverages reactive forms and an in-house UI framework to produce a modernized experience for loan apps, allowing bankers to move away from an older platform. The backend logic in the .NET microservice obscures the complicated data models required by the legacy systems which process loan applications into a usable API.

In my first year, I helped support M&T's customer facing iOS Mobile Banking application. During the year, I updated monitoring tools and leveraged them to reduce app crashes and fix bugs. I also worked on efforts to implement a new 3rd party authentication flow into the app, and integrate a new version of an API for making payments from an external bank. I also took lead on writing Jira test cases for validating new features and fixes.

positions.title: Peer Leader
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States · On-site
positions.description: I taught weekly seminars to introduce students to various topics in Computer Science. During the 75 minute duration of class, this included both lecturing and guiding students through interactive activities and discussions.

company.name: Columbia University Department of Computer Science

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States · Hybrid
positions.description:
I worked on research in applying QD algorithms to Procedural Content Generation.
During Barnard's 2023 Summer Research Institute, I developed an environment in Python to virtually represent and evolve lego structures.

positions.title: Computer Science Tutor
positions.description: I worked as a tutor in Barnard's Computer Science help room, aiding students in introductory and intermediate CS courses to understand material and homework.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States · Remote
positions.description: I worked part-time with a startup through Columbia Build Lab, a program which matches students with MBA founders. Specifically, I contributed to the SwiftUI frontend for the startup's mobile application.

positions.title: Workshop Assistant
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States · On-site
positions.description: I assisted weekly seminars for introductory Computer Science students by engaging students in discussion, sending out logistical information, and presenting lectures when the peer leader is absent.

company.name: Columbia University Department of Computer Science

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description: I conducted research through the NSF-funded Immersive Media Computing REU at GSU. I worked for 8 weeks with a mentor on research to create First Person View goggles for a drone via an Android app. This develop my knowledge of Computer Vision, VR, and mobile development. In the end, I produced a final report, poster, and presentation summarizing my work and results.
positions.insights: Skills: TensorFlow · OpenCV · Mobile Applications · Drones · Android Development · Computer Vision · Research · Java

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States
positions.description: Through Barnard College's 2021 Summer Research Institute, I worked on developing a mobile application designed to help adolescents manage their mental health. Created for use in a study by Columbia's School of Social Work, I collaborated on the application with a team of other students. My main role was in developing a CBT (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy) module for the app.
positions.insights: Skills: Flutter · Mobile Applications · Research · Figma (Software)
